newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS --prices stumble with T-bonds.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS --prices stumble with T-bonds.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were caught in Treasuries' downdraft on Monday, falling four to five basis points, as a variety of indicators signalled the economy was a bit stronger than anticipated.
"There's a little bit of a heavy tone, we're following Treasuries. All the economic (reports) have come out looking like a stronger economy," a trader said.

The market already was on edge because the Federal Reserve's policy body starts a two-day meeting on Tuesday, and while economists last week were confident the central bank would leave rates unchanged, the surprising strength in the economy was worrisome.
Further, the June payrolls data, which can rock markets if its findings prove surprising, were due out on Thursday, one day early, due to the U.S. Independence Day holiday on Friday.
Municipal bonds, which had been correcting slightly from strong gains achieved vis a vis Treasury bonds, on Monday outshone their sister bonds a bit, traders said.

"I think they underperformed in the last couple of weeks, but today actually outperformed," a trader said. This is not uncommon on volatile trading days, as municipal bonds are much less liquid than Treasuries, and traders tend to be slower to mark them up or down.

Trading was fairly slow, partly because a number of players were vacationing, taking advantage of Friday's holiday. A number of issuers were said to be postponning sales slated for this week until next week.

Among the data depressing prices was the Chicago Purchasers Index, which jumped to 61.5 in June, sharply higher than forecasts for a slight drop from May's 56.8 level to 56.4. An index below 50 signals a slowing manufacturing economy, while a reading above 50 points to an expansion.

And a big uptick in May home sales also hurt, as they rose 7.1 percent to an annual rate of 825,000. Only a rate of 786,000 units had been expected. And May's 4.1 months' supply of homes for sales was the lowest amount since March 1971.
In the secondary market, Atlanta, Georgia's Water and Sewer Revenues of 2027, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.60 percent, NET, up one basis point.
And Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority Massachusetts General Transportation of March 2023, which pay a five percent coupon, were bid at 5.63 percent, up three basis points.
